spec.title: Allowed DNS — $network / ${host:text}
spec.description: Resolved DNS queries not blocked for the selected network and host.

spec.expr:
{nodename="$network"}
|= "query resolved"
| logfmt
| __error__ = ""
| response_reason != "BLOCKED"
| question_name != ""
| question_name != "unifi."
| client_ip =~ "^${host:raw}$"
| line_format `{{ .question_name | trimSuffix "." }}  ·  client={{ .client_names | default .client_ip }}  ·  ip={{ .client_ip }}  ·  type={{ .question_type }}  ·  rcode={{ .response_code }}`

spec.title: DNS query volume and blocked percentage (15m rolling) — $network / ${host:text}
spec.description: Total and blocked DNS queries over a rolling 15-minute window, with blocked percentage over the same window on the right axis.

spec.expr:
sum(
  count_over_time(
    {nodename="$network"}
    |= "query resolved"
    | logfmt
    | __error__ = ""
    | question_name != ""
    | client_ip =~ "^${host:raw}$"
    [15m]
  )
)

sum(
  count_over_time(
    {nodename="$network"}
    |= "query resolved"
    |= "response_reason=BLOCKED"
    | logfmt
    | __error__ = ""
    | response_reason = "BLOCKED"
    | question_name != ""
    | client_ip =~ "^${host:raw}$"
    [15m]
  )
)

100 *
sum(
  count_over_time(
    {nodename="$network"}
    |= "query resolved"
    |= "response_reason=BLOCKED"
    | logfmt
    | __error__ = ""
    | response_reason = "BLOCKED"
    | question_name != ""
    | client_ip =~ "^${host:raw}$"
    [15m]
  )
)
/
sum(
  count_over_time(
    {nodename="$network"}
    |= "query resolved"
    | logfmt
    | __error__ = ""
    | question_name != ""
    | client_ip =~ "^${host:raw}$"
    [15m]
  )
)

spec.title: Cached percentage — $network / ${host:text}
spec.description: Percentage of resolved DNS queries served from Blocky's cache.

spec.expr:
100 *
sum(
  count_over_time(
    {nodename="$network"}
    |= "query resolved"
    | logfmt
    | __error__ = ""
    | response_type = "CACHED"
    | question_name != ""
    | client_ip =~ "^${host:raw}$"
    [$__range]
  )
)
/
sum(
  count_over_time(
    {nodename="$network"}
    |= "query resolved"
    | logfmt
    | __error__ = ""
    | question_name != ""
    | client_ip =~ "^${host:raw}$"
    [$__range]
  )
)

spec.title: Queries by DNS record type
spec.description: Distribution of A, AAAA, HTTPS, PTR and other DNS question types.

spec.expr:
sum by (question_type) (
  count_over_time(
    {nodename="$network"}
    |= "query resolved"
    | logfmt
    | __error__ = ""
    | question_type != ""
    | client_ip =~ "^${host:raw}$"
    [$__range]
  )
)

spec.title: Queries by client
spec.description: Top 15 DNS clients by query volume.

spec.expr:
topk(
  15,
  sum by (client_names, client_ip) (
    count_over_time(
      {nodename="$network"}
      |= "query resolved"
      | logfmt
      | __error__ = ""
      | client_ip != ""
      | client_ip =~ "^${host:raw}$"
      [$__range]
    )
  )
)

spec.title: Blocked queries by blocklist group
spec.description: Blocky group or group combination responsible for each blocked response.

spec.expr:
sum by (block_group) (
  count_over_time(
    {nodename="$network"}
    |= "query resolved"
    |= "response_reason=BLOCKED"
    | logfmt
    | __error__ = ""
    | response_reason = "BLOCKED"
    | client_ip =~ "^${host:raw}$"
    | regexp `response_reason=BLOCKED(?: \((?P<block_group>[^)]+)\))?`
    | block_group != ""
    [$__range]
  )
)

spec.title: Response reasons
spec.description: Top-level Blocky response reason extracted from each query log entry.

spec.expr:
sum by (reason) (
  count_over_time(
    {nodename="$network"}
    |= "query resolved"
    | regexp `response_reason=(?P<reason>[A-Z_]+)`
    | reason != ""
    | logfmt
    | __error__ = ""
    | client_ip =~ "^${host:raw}$"
    [$__range]
  )
)

spec.title: Response type
spec.description: Blocky response categories such as resolved, cached and blocked.

spec.expr:
sum by (response_type) (
  count_over_time(
    {nodename="$network"}
    |= "query resolved"
    | logfmt
    | __error__ = ""
    | response_type != ""
    | client_ip =~ "^${host:raw}$"
    [$__range]
  )
)

spec.title: DNS response status
spec.description: DNS return codes such as NOERROR, NXDOMAIN and SERVFAIL.

spec.expr:
sum by (response_code) (
  count_over_time(
    {nodename="$network"}
    |= "query resolved"
    | logfmt
    | __error__ = ""
    | response_code != ""
    | client_ip =~ "^${host:raw}$"
    [$__range]
  )
)

spec.title: Average DNS response time — $network / ${host:text}
spec.description: Mean Blocky query duration for the selected time range.

spec.expr:
avg(
  avg_over_time(
    {nodename="$network"}
    |= "query resolved"
    | logfmt
    | question_name != ""
    | client_ip =~ "^${host:raw}$"
    | unwrap duration_ms
    | __error__ = ""
    [$__range]
  )
)

spec.title: Active clients — $network / ${host:text}
spec.description: Distinct client IPs that made DNS queries in the selected time range.

spec.expr:
count(
  sum by (client_ip) (
    count_over_time(
      {nodename="$network"}
      |= "query resolved"
      | logfmt
      | __error__ = ""
      | question_name != ""
      | client_ip != ""
      | client_ip =~ "^${host:raw}$"
      [$__range]
    )
  )
)

spec.title: Receive rate — $network / ${interface:text}
spec.description: Current aggregate inbound traffic rate across the selected interface scope.

spec.title: Transmit rate — $network / ${interface:text}
spec.description: Current aggregate outbound traffic rate across the selected interface scope.

spec.title: Packet rate — $network / ${interface:text}
spec.description: Combined inbound and outbound packet rate.

spec.title: Errors + drops — $network / ${interface:text}
spec.description: Combined receive/transmit errors and dropped packets per second.

spec.expr: sum(rate(node_network_receive_errs_total{instance="${node:raw}", device=~"^${interface:raw}$", device!~"lo|veth.*|docker.*"}[5m])) + sum(rate(node_network_transmit_errs_total{instance="${node:raw}", device=~"^${interface:raw}$", device!~"lo|veth.*|docker.*"}[5m])) + sum(rate(node_network_receive_drop_total{instance="${node:raw}", device=~"^${interface:raw}$", device!~"lo|veth.*|docker.*"}[5m])) + sum(rate(node_network_transmit_drop_total{instance="${node:raw}", device=~"^${interface:raw}$", device!~"lo|veth.*|docker.*"}[5m]))

spec.title: Network traffic — $network / ${interface:text}
spec.description: Inbound traffic is positive; outbound traffic is mirrored below zero for rapid comparison.

spec.title: Link utilisation — $network / ${interface:text}
spec.description: Traffic as a fraction of the interface speed reported by node_exporter; virtual and PPP links may not expose a speed.

spec.expr: (node_network_speed_bytes{instance="${node:raw}", device=~"^${interface:raw}$", device!~"lo|veth.*|docker.*"} > bool 0) * (rate(node_network_receive_bytes_total{instance="${node:raw}", device=~"^${interface:raw}$", device!~"lo|veth.*|docker.*"}[5m]) / node_network_speed_bytes{instance="${node:raw}", device=~"^${interface:raw}$", device!~"lo|veth.*|docker.*"})

(node_network_speed_bytes{instance="${node:raw}", device=~"^${interface:raw}$", device!~"lo|veth.*|docker.*"} > bool 0) * (rate(node_network_transmit_bytes_total{instance="${node:raw}", device=~"^${interface:raw}$", device!~"lo|veth.*|docker.*"}[5m]) / node_network_speed_bytes{instance="${node:raw}", device=~"^${interface:raw}$", device!~"lo|veth.*|docker.*"})

spec.title: Packets per second — $network / ${interface:text}
spec.description: Inbound and outbound packet rates per interface.

spec.title: Interface errors and drops — $network / ${interface:text}
spec.description: Receive/transmit errors and drops per second, separated by interface.

spec.title: Blocked DNS — $network / ${host:text}
spec.description: Blocked DNS queries with the matched block group for the selected network and host.

spec.expr:
{nodename="$network"}
|= "query resolved"
|= "response_reason=BLOCKED"
!= "stats.grafana.org"
| logfmt
| __error__ = ""
| response_reason = "BLOCKED"
| question_name != ""
| client_ip =~ "^${host:raw}$"
| regexp `response_reason=BLOCKED(?: \((?P<block_group>[^)]+)\))?`
| line_format `{{ .question_name | trimSuffix "." }}  ·  client={{ .client_names | default .client_ip }}  ·  ip={{ .client_ip }}  ·  type={{ .question_type }}  ·  group={{ .block_group | default "-" }}`

spec.title: IP firewall blocks — $network / ${host:text}
spec.description: Firewall block events sourced by the selected client IP.

spec.expr:
{nodename="$network"} |~ `nft-block-(feed|local|doh|port) `
| regexp `(?P<kind>nft-block-[a-z]+) .*SRC=(?P<src>[^ ]+) DST=(?P<dst>[^ ]+)`
| src =~ "^${host:raw}$"
| dst != ""
| regexp `PROTO=(?P<proto>[A-Z]+)`
| regexp `DPT=(?P<dport>[0-9]+)`
| line_format `{{ .kind }}  ·  {{ .src }} → {{ .dst }}{{ if .dport }}:{{ .dport }}{{ end }}  ·  {{ .proto }}`

spec.title: IP block types — $network / ${host:text}
spec.description: Stacked firewall block counts by nftables block category.

spec.title: Top 20 blocked domains — $network / ${host:text}
spec.description: Most frequently blocked DNS names in the selected time range.

spec.expr:
topk(

  sum by (question_name) (

      |= "response_reason=BLOCKED"
      != "stats.grafana.org"
      | logfmt
      | __error__ = ""
      | response_reason = "BLOCKED"

      | client_ip =~ "^${host:raw}$"

)

spec.title: CAKE tins — $network
spec.description: One row per shaper tin. Throughput is what the tin is carrying; threshold is the rate above which CAKE stops giving it priority and falls back to serving it by weight. Voice sitting well under its threshold is the condition prioritisation depends on.

spec.title: Tin throughput — $network
spec.description: Traffic carried by each CAKE tin. Calls marked by the qos-mark chain appear in Voice; everything unclassified sits in Best Effort.

spec.title: Tin average delay — $network
spec.description: Sojourn time inside each tin, straight from CAKE. This is the panel that answers whether prioritisation is working: Voice should stay flat and low while Best Effort climbs under load.

spec.title: Penalty classes — $network
spec.description: The HTB classes that the throttle and imo lists steer into. These bypass CAKE entirely, so they never appear in the tin panels above.

spec.title: Classification rules — $network
spec.description: Match rate of each rule in the nftables qos-mark chain. A rule sitting at zero when it should not be is the fastest way to spot classification that has silently stopped matching — the STUN signature especially.

spec.title: VPN throttle — download now
spec.description: Current inbound rate through the throttle class, measured on the LAN egress shaper.

spec.title: VPN throttle — upload now
spec.description: Current outbound rate through the throttle class, measured on the PPP egress shaper.

spec.title: imo throttle — download now
spec.description: Current inbound rate through the imo class, measured on the LAN egress shaper.

spec.title: imo throttle — upload now
spec.description: Current outbound rate through the imo class, measured on the PPP egress shaper.

spec.title: VPN throttle throughput vs cap — $network
spec.description: Traffic actually getting through the throttle class in each direction, against the HTB rate cap configured for it. Sitting flat on the cap means the tier is saturated and the shaper is the binding constraint.

spec.title: imo throttle throughput vs cap — $network
spec.description: Traffic actually getting through the imo class in each direction, against the HTB rate cap configured for it. Sitting flat on the cap means the tier is saturated and the shaper is the binding constraint.

spec.title: Throttle drop rate — $network
spec.description: Packets discarded inside each penalty class — the HTB cap plus the netem loss applied on top of it. This is the throttling being felt, as opposed to merely configured.

spec.title: Rate-cap pressure — $network
spec.description: How often each penalty class asked for more than its rate allows. Overlimits climbing while drops stay low means traffic is being delayed into the cap rather than discarded.

spec.title: Throttled queue backlog — $network
spec.description: Bytes sitting in each penalty class waiting to be dequeued. A persistent backlog is the latency a throttled app experiences; netem's queue is bounded at 1000 packets, so what will not fit is dropped instead.

spec.title: Throttle rule matches — $network
spec.description: Match rate of each rule in the nftables forward_throttle chain, which is where the throttle and imo sets are turned into a firewall mark. This is the only per-direction and per-address-family view of the two tiers — both families and both directions collapse into one HTB class once marked. A rule flat at zero while its tier shows traffic means the other family is carrying it. Addresses added at runtime with `tempthrottle` are counted here too: it writes into the same throttle4/throttle6 sets these rules match on, so its traffic is already in these lines — the panel below is what separates a live addition from the listed ones.

spec.title: VPN indicators — $network / ${host:text}
spec.description: Counts over the selected range. Any non-zero value is worth reading the detail panels for; none of these are normal for a device with no VPN, proxy or tunnel app installed.

spec.title: Devices ranked by VPN indicators — $network
spec.description: One bar per device over the selected range, highest first. Combines STUN discovery, resolver bypass, VPN-list and curated-list hits. Deliberately not filtered by the host picker: this is the panel that tells you which host to pick.

spec.expr:
topk(
  20,
  sum by (client_names, client_ip) (
    count_over_time(
      {nodename="$network"}
      |= "query resolved"
      |~ `question_name=stun\.|response_reason=BLOCKED \([^)]*(doh|vpn|custom)`
      | logfmt
      | __error__ = ""
      | client_ip != ""
      [$__range]
    )
  )
)

links.title: Filter the Inspection tab to this device
Peers and actions on the router (mesh only)

spec.title: Bypass attempts over time — ${host:text}
spec.description: The same four indicators as a rate. A tunnel client that has just lost its node shows a burst of discovery here.

spec.title: Top blocked names — ${host:text}
spec.description: What the selected device is being denied. Tunnel and imo control-plane names surface here before any traffic-side signal exists.

spec.expr:
topk(25,
  sum by (question_name) (
    count_over_time(
      {nodename="$network"}
      |= "query resolved"
      |= "response_reason=BLOCKED"
      | logfmt
      | __error__ = ""
      | client_ip =~ "^${host:raw}$"
      | question_name != ""
      [$__range]
    )
  )
)

spec.title: DNS query rate — ${host:text}
spec.description: Total resolver activity for the device. A handset that keeps moving traffic while this falls to near zero is reaching addresses it never looked up, which is the shape of a tunnel dialling a cached endpoint.

spec.title: Top-peer share by device — $network
spec.description: The share of a device's currently tracked bytes held by its single largest peer. This is the discriminator every tunnel on this network has been found by: a tunnel peer holds 70-100%, the same device browsing normally sits at 20-35%. Requires the host-flow collector.

links.title: Filter the Inspection tab to this device
Peers and actions on the router (mesh only)

spec.title: Peer count by device — $network
spec.description: Distinct peers each device currently holds flows with. The companion to the share panel and the thing that separates a tunnel from a large download: a device pulling video from one CDN still talks to dozens of other hosts, a tunnelled device often talks to one.

links.title: Filter the Inspection tab to this device
Peers and actions on the router (mesh only)

spec.title: Traffic by device — $network
spec.description: Per-host throughput from the nftables element counters. Unlike the share figures above these are monotonic counters and survive the flows that produced them, so this is the panel to read for volume over time.

links.title: Filter the Inspection tab to this device
Peers and actions on the router (mesh only)

spec.title: Temporary blocks in force — $network
spec.description: Addresses currently carrying a `tempblock` rule on this router. These are ad-hoc drops added by hand or from the peers page; they live in their own nftables table, survive a rebuild, and are only cleared by `tempblock del` or `tempblock flush`.

spec.title: Temporary blocks — hits by address — $network
spec.description: Drop rate of each `tempblock` rule, by address and direction. to-peer climbing while from-peer sits at zero is a working block against an app that has not given up; both at zero means the address has been left behind and can be released. Unlike the panels above this is not filtered by ${host:text} — a firewall drop counter records the peer, not which client was talking to it.

spec.title: Temporary block hits over time — $network
spec.description: The ten busiest `tempblock` rules over the selected window. This is where an app moving between endpoints shows itself: one address falling to zero while another appears is the same app re-homing, not the block working.

spec.title: Throttled addresses — $network
spec.description: How many addresses each throttle set holds. The rule counters above say how much traffic is being marked, not how much is in scope, and these sets have two writers: a rebuild repopulates them from custom-throttle-list.txt, while `tempthrottle add` and `del` change them live. A step here with no rebuild is a temporary throttle going on or coming off.

spec.title: Downloaded in range — $network / ${interface:text}
spec.description: Total inbound traffic across the selected interface scope. Volume rather than rate: this counts the whole of the time range selected in the picker, so it changes when the range does. Bytes, where the rate stats above are bits.

spec.title: Uploaded in range — $network / ${interface:text}
spec.description: Total outbound traffic across the selected interface scope. Volume rather than rate: this counts the whole of the time range selected in the picker, so it changes when the range does. Bytes, where the rate stats above are bits.

spec.title: Total in range — $network / ${interface:text}
spec.description: Inbound plus outbound across the selected interface scope. Volume rather than rate: this counts the whole of the time range selected in the picker, so it changes when the range does. Bytes, where the rate stats above are bits. On a router the same traffic is normally counted twice — once entering on one interface and once leaving on another — so this is only a link total while a single interface is selected.

spec.title: CDN quota — over-cap throughput — $network
spec.description: Traffic from low-trust pool devices to CDN space AFTER that device has exhausted its volume quota, split by direction and address family. This is the only view that separates the CDN quota from the VPN throttle: the quota's rules end in `meta mark set 0x2`, the same mark forward_throttle sets, so once marked both land in HTB class 1:20 and the "VPN throttle" panels above count them together. Subtract this from panel 124 to get genuine tunnel-node traffic. Zero here does NOT mean the quota is off — it means no pool device has gone over its allowance, which is the expected state. Check the panel to the right for whether any device is in scope at all. Absent entirely on a router with cdnQuota disabled (bongo today).

spec.title: CDN quota — pool devices in scope — $network
spec.description: Number of per-device token buckets currently held in cdn_over4/cdn_over6. READ THIS CAREFULLY: an element is created for every pool device that touches CDN space at all, because that is where its token bucket lives — so this counts devices WITH A CDN BUDGET, not devices over quota. Going over is what the panel to the left measures. A flat non-zero line here with nothing on the left is the quota working silently: devices are being metered and none has exhausted its allowance. Entries reap on a 2h idle timeout and the sets are capped at size 1024, so a line pinned at 1024 means the set is full and new devices are not being metered — that is a real fault, not a busy night.
